focus.label: Malignant thyroid tumor is papillary thyroid carcinoma
focus.why: Current frontier 'malignant thyroid tumor' is a broad category requiring histologic subtype refinement. Papillary carcinoma is the most common thyroid malignancy in young adults and fits the cervical lymphadenopathy, rapid growth of a long-standing nodular goiter, and firm grade III gland (node-3, node-5). Expert pathologist analysis favors papillary carcinoma as the leading subtype (node-11, node-14), while normal calcitonin and antibodies refute medullary and autoimmune etiologies (node-4).
